page_title: Mask R-CNN in OpenCV: Detection and Segmentation

summary.title: Mask R-CNN in OpenCV: Detection and Segmentation
summary.one_liner: You learn how to run a pretrained Mask R-CNN (TensorFlow Inception V2, COCO) through OpenCV's DNN module in Python and C++ to get per-object binary masks, not just bounding boxes.
takeaways: Mask R-CNN adds a mask prediction branch to Faster R-CNN, so each detected object gets a greyscale mask that can be thresholded into a binary mask.
Load the TensorFlow frozen graph and its pbtxt text graph with cv.dnn.readNetFromTensorflow, then set the OpenCV backend and CPU target.
Preprocess each frame with blobFromImage (swapRB=True), run forward on 'detection_out_final' and 'detection_masks', then filter boxes by confidence and threshold masks.
Confidence threshold (0.5) filters boxes; mask threshold (0.3) controls mask size, with lower values giving larger masks.
summary.summary: The post explains instance segmentation and the evolution from R-CNN to Fast, Faster and Mask R-CNN, then walks through a Mask R-CNN pipeline in OpenCV. Steps cover downloading the TensorFlow Inception V2 COCO model, setting confidence and mask thresholds, loading the network and class/colour files, reading image, video or webcam input, and running a forward pass with blob preprocessing. It also shows the post-processing that filters boxes, resizes and thresholds masks, and draws boxes, coloured overlays and contours, with code given in both Python and C++. The author reports CPU inference of about 350 ms to 2 s per frame on a Mac with an Intel Core i7.
